# `apps/realmforge/modeler/compile/AssemblyCompiler.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/apps/realmforge/modeler/compile/AssemblyCompiler.js`

AssemblyCompiler.js — compiles a validated ForgeSource STRUCTURE GRAPH into geometry. Semantic first, geometry derived: parts + parents form the graph; repeat/mirror are generator ops expanded here (with provenance); vertices come exclusively from registered Engine geometry generators — this file generates NO vertex math of its own beyond baking world transforms. Output `model` is EngineModel-shaped ({ name, primitives:[{ attributes: { position, normal }, indices, vertexCount }] }) so the existing AssetExporter (OBJ/PLY/STL/GLB) and MeshBoundsReader consume it unchanged (rest-pose, world-baked). Nodes carry LOCAL meshes + world matrices (dims baked, transform in the matrix) so the viewport can move/animate parts by rewriting matrices — gizmo drags and motion playback never re-upload vertices. The `rig` output (topo-ordered parts, base TRS, compiled motion ASTs, per-node generator provenance) is what motion/MotionRuntime.js evaluates per frame.

## Functions

### `composeTRS(pos, rot, scale, pivot = null)`

Compose a TRS matrix (rot in degrees, applied Z·Y·X, then scale). An optional `pivot` (local point) makes the rotation ORBIT that point instead of the part origin: T(pos)·T(piv)·R·T(-piv)·S. With pivot [0,0,0] this is the plain T·R·S, so unpivoted parts are unchanged. Used for e.g. a flipper bat that must rotate about the shaft, not its own centre.

### `compileAssembly(source, { resolvedMaterials = null, textures = null } = {})`

Compile the canonical pipeline synchronously for existing callers.

**Parameters:**

- `source` *(string|object)* — ForgeSource text or doc
- `[options]` *(object)* — Optional resolved material and texture collections.

**Returns:** {{ ok:boolean, errors:string[], warnings:string[], model:object|null,

### `async compileAssemblyCooperative(source, { checkpoint, ...options } = {})`

Compile the same pipeline with owner-provided scheduling and cancellation. Each checkpoint receives only the CPU time of one generator segment; waits are excluded. Geometry generators themselves remain synchronous operations. The owner must snapshot inputs before allowing caller mutation during awaits.

### `applyGen(gen, partWorld)`

Derive an instance world matrix from its generator record + the part world.
